providers.name: entity.game.bomb_planted
providers.note: True from the frame the bomb is planted, and cleared by a defuse as well as at round_officially_ended, so it is not "the bomb was planted this round": that is `round.bomb.was_planted`, which stays true to the round's end.

providers.name: entity.game.game_phase
providers.note: The match phase. Measured on matchmaking demos: 2 through the first half, 4 over the halftime break, 3 through the second half, 5 once the match is over.

providers.name: entity.game.round_time
providers.note: The length the round is configured to run, not a countdown: 115 in a live matchmaking round, 999 during warmup.

providers.name: entity.game.round_win_reason
providers.note: The engine's round-end reason, set with round_win_status and cleared with it: 7 bomb defused, 8 counter-terrorists eliminated the terrorists, 9 terrorists eliminated the counter-terrorists, 12 target saved (time ran out). 0 while the round is undecided. Read it on the `round_decided` view (its `reason` facet) or between the decision and the round's close, never on `round_ended`, where it has already reset to 0; there, `enrich.round.win_reason` carries it.

providers.name: entity.game.round_win_status
providers.note: 0 while the round is undecided, 2 once the terrorists have won it, 3 once the counter-terrorists have. It goes 0 to 2/3 on the frame the round is decided and back to 0 at round_officially_ended, 448 ticks later on matchmaking demos, so on `round_ended` it reads 0. The `round_decided` view fires on the step, and at the round's close the winner is `enrich.round.winner_side`.

providers.name: entity.game.total_rounds_played
providers.note: Rounds decided so far this match: 0 before round 1, and it increments on the frame a round is decided, not when the next one starts.

providers.name: entity.pawn.duck_amount
providers.note: Continuous over 0..1, not a flag: it ramps across the crouch transition, so a threshold on it reads as "how far into the crouch", not "is crouching".

providers.name: entity.pawn.eye_pitch
providers.note: CS2's convention: NEGATIVE is up. Wraps, so subtract two of these only after normalising the difference.

providers.name: entity.pawn.eye_yaw
providers.note: Counter-clockwise from world +X, and it wraps at 360, so subtract two of these only after normalising the difference.

providers.name: entity.pawn.flash_duration
providers.note: The duration the server LATCHED for the flash, not a countdown: probed on the bundled GOTV sample it holds one value for the whole blind and then steps to 0, and the step is about 1.4x the latched value after the flash, so it never reads as "time still blind". Use `> 0` for "is blinded"; a magnitude test on it measures the flash, not what is left of it.

providers.name: entity.pawn.max_speed
providers.note: Per-weapon (an AWP out caps far lower than a knife), which is what makes it the denominator of a counter-strafe test rather than a fixed speed.

providers.name: entity.pawn.punch_pitch
providers.note: NOT USABLE AS RECOIL TODAY. It is the raw aim-punch spring sample, correct only at its own base tick, and on the bundled GOTV sample it does not decode to degrees of punch at all: the two components cluster near -94 and +89, which no weapon's kick reaches. The engine's own consumer rejects every value outside +/-45 for that reason. A threshold on this column is true on nearly every tick and means nothing about recoil.

providers.name: entity.pawn.punch_yaw
providers.note: NOT USABLE AS RECOIL TODAY, for the reasons under `player.punch_pitch`: same raw spring sample, same undecoded cluster on the bundled sample, same rejection by the engine's own consumer.

providers.name: entity.pawn.shots_fired
providers.note: Position within the CURRENT burst, not a round or match total: it resets on trigger release and on weapon change.

providers.name: entity.weapon.accuracy_penalty
providers.note: A raw engine accumulator in no unit, scaled per weapon: the same number means a different spread on a Deagle and on a Negev, so compare it within one weapon and never across two. It also excludes the movement term, so a running player's shot is more inaccurate than this says. For the movement term itself, ask the `shot_landed` view instead: its counter-strafe facets are lowered from `bullet_damage.InaccuracyMove`, which is the penalty the server actually charged the shot, and no entity read can better it. This column is the accumulator as it stood BEFORE the frame, which is the only answer available on a demo that emits no `bullet_damage` and the only one available at all for a shot that missed.

providers.name: entity.weapon.recoil_index
providers.note: A raw engine accumulator in no unit, scaled per weapon. Its useful property is that it rises within a spray and falls between sprays (a run over which it never drops is one spray), not its absolute magnitude, which is not comparable across weapons. Not the same number as the `recoil_index` FACET on `shot_landed`: that one is `bullet_damage.RecoilIndex`, the index the server fired the shot at, and is authoritative for "what did this shot fire at". This column is the entity read as it stood BEFORE the frame, so it answers "where was the spray up to when the shot site fired" and is the only answer on a demo carrying no `bullet_damage` or for a shot that missed. Do not pool the two in one stat.

views.name: enemy_spotted
views.note: Synthesized from visibility sampling, so event.tick is the FRAME clock, not the absolute server tick a wire event carries: differencing it against a kill or shot tick adds the demo's ServerStartTick (about 20,000). Use the ticks_since_* facets for timing across views.

views.name: molotov
views.note: Synthesized from entity state, so event.tick is the FRAME clock, not the absolute server tick a wire event carries: differencing it against a kill or bomb_planted tick adds the demo's ServerStartTick (about 20,000). Use the ticks_since_* facets for timing across views.

views.name: round_decided
views.note: Synthesized from the game rules' round-win status on the frame the round is decided, so event.tick is the FRAME clock, the same value event.frame_tick reads. Fires once per decided round, after the frame's own events; the round's close (round_ended) comes 448 ticks later on a matchmaking demo.
